[vc_row row_height_percent="0" override_padding="yes" h_padding="2" top_padding="4" bottom_padding="0" overlay_alpha="100" gutter_size="3" column_width_percent="100" shift_y="0" z_index="0" row_height_use_pixel="" uncode_shortcode_id="282890"][vc_column column_width_percent="100" position_horizontal="left" gutter_size="3" overlay_alpha="50" shift_x="0" shift_y="0" shift_y_down="0" z_index="0" medium_width="0" mobile_width="0" css_animation="left-t-right" zoom_width="0" zoom_height="0" uncode_shortcode_id="931923"][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="437224"]Todays designers are under intense pressure to achieve unicorn status. Create a podcast now. Learn to be a "thinking leader," whatever that means. Designers must acquire new abilities to succeed in todays competitive design industry. Coding is a skill that is in high demand.n
A lot of people are concerned about this. If you type "should designers" into Google, thats the best indicator. Six of the most popular search queries address the question of whether or not designers need to know how to code.
nThe ability to write code is optional to be a successful digital designer. But, you should be familiar with the processes behind the creation and upkeep of digital products. Paints may be mixed to create new hues, and artists have this skill down well. Professional cooks have an arsenal of spices at their disposal. Any digital designer worth their salt will have a deep working knowledge of the technologies they use.[/vc_column_text][vc_single_image media="118773" media_width_percent="100" uncode_shortcode_id="113016"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent="0" override_padding="yes" h_padding="2" top_padding="3" bottom_padding="3" overlay_alpha="100" gutter_size="3" shift_y="0" row_height_use_pixel=""][vc_column column_width_percent="100" gutter_size="3" overlay_alpha="50" shift_x="0" shift_y="0" shift_y_down="0" z_index="0" medium_width="0" mobile_width="0" css_animation="left-t-right" zoom_width="0" zoom_height="0" uncode_shortcode_id="192618"][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h4" text_size="h4" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" uncode_shortcode_id="208768"]What do we mean by "code."[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="431390"]n

There is a tendency to generalise all programmers in the same way that one may generalise all designers. Developers can differ significantly in how they approach problems, their chosen processes, and the areas in which they may have developed expertise.

n

If youre a designer working with developers, you must have a firm grasp of what they do and the environment in which they operate.

n[/vc_column_text][vc_single_image media="118777" media_width_percent="100" uncode_shortcode_id="308885"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent="0" override_padding="yes" h_padding="2" top_padding="3" bottom_padding="3" overlay_alpha="100" gutter_size="3" shift_y="0" row_height_use_pixel=""][vc_column column_width_percent="100" gutter_size="2" overlay_alpha="50" shift_x="0" shift_y="0" shift_y_down="0" z_index="0" medium_width="0" mobile_width="0" css_animation="left-t-right" zoom_width="0" zoom_height="0" uncode_shortcode_id="830254"][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h3" text_size="h3" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" sub_lead="yes" sub_reduced="yes" uncode_shortcode_id="458191" subheading="Developers need to break out the parts of a design to learn how to put it together."]What goes on behind the screen?[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="141796"]There are many steps between approving our ideas and seeing the finished output from the developers. When compared to humans, their thought processes are distinct. Yet, we can still have a conversation with them.nnIve managed to avoid learning everything there is to know this far. Im sure Ill always be an expert on everything related to technology, as there are so many areas in which I need to be more knowledgeable. Because I want to keep things straightforward, Ill go through the most memorable and helpful bits. There are essentially only three factors at play here:n

  • How does our interface gets built?

n

n[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row row_height_percent="0" override_padding="yes" h_padding="2" top_padding="3" bottom_padding="3" overlay_alpha="100" gutter_size="3" column_width_percent="100" shift_y="0" z_index="0" row_height_use_pixel="" uncode_shortcode_id="205726"][vc_column column_width_percent="100" gutter_size="3" overlay_alpha="50" shift_x="0" shift_y="0" shift_y_down="0" z_index="0" medium_width="0" mobile_width="0" css_animation="left-t-right" zoom_width="0" zoom_height="0" uncode_shortcode_id="150403"][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h3" text_size="h3" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" sub_lead="yes" sub_reduced="yes" uncode_shortcode_id="400728" subheading="When we surf online, there is a lot of communication happening across the Internet between various devices worldwide."]Components of the system[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="708253"]n

The data we collect is stored on hundreds of servers in dozens of countries. Information may be transmitted worldwide in seconds using towers and satellites in Earths orbit. Thousands of miles of underwater cable carry gigabytes of data per second.

n

Unfortunately, we can only take in the world through our screens. Thats fine, by the way.

n

We arent engineers, so we arent usually the ones that handle it as designers to worry about how these relationships work. All that matters to us is providing helpful information to our customers as quickly and painlessly as possible.

n[/vc_column_text][vc_single_image media="118973" media_width_percent="100" uncode_shortcode_id="175656"][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="115614"]In my career as a digital designer, Ive gotten by with the following knowledge:nnInterface design is our domain—location of controls, choice of aesthetic palette, and responsiveness to input. We have the right to make and enforce these policies. When we give developers our designs, they turn them into code.nnClients are what you use to construct and show user interfaces to end users. This is a catch-all phrase for any computer an individual uses. Mobile devices, computers, and electronic tablets. Devices of this type have adequate power to do some fundamental tasks but need help under greater demands. Try putting your phone into "Airplane" mode to see how ineffective it is, and youll get the idea.nnServers can be viewed as the "brains" of a product. These devices are large and robust enough to do complex tasks. To access data, client devices must communicate with servers over the Internet. A client will contact a server for resources when it needs them. Servers also have an advantage in speed when it comes to sophisticated tasks.nnInformation exchange between client and server must occur over the Internet. With the help of machines like yours, data can be transferred quickly around the globe.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column column_width_percent="100" gutter_size="2" overlay_alpha="50" shift_x="0" shift_y="0" shift_y_down="0" z_index="0" medium_width="0" mobile_width="0" css_animation="left-t-right" width="1/1" uncode_shortcode_id="196341"][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h3" text_size="h3" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" sub_lead="yes" sub_reduced="yes" uncode_shortcode_id="245237" el_id="H3" el_class="H3" subheading="The ``stack`` of a product is its collection of interdependent parts. Its environment is vast and intricate."]The technology stack[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="163420"]Among the best analogies Ive come across from The Software Guild is to picture the IT stack as a burger. A burger must have specific ingredients, but the rest of the sandwich can be customised to the eaters preferences. The burger in your product might have onions on it, or it might not. The patties were made by one programmer and the cheese by another.nnMany technologies may make up the stack used by your design team. One example of a "design stack" might be the programmes Sketch, Framer X, Zeplin, Abstract, Adobe Illustrator, and Origami. You may replace Sketch with another programme, such as Figma. You may use Adobe XD to pool the talents of multiple designers.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column column_width_percent="100" gutter_size="3" overlay_alpha="50" shift_x="0" shift_y="0" shift_y_down="0" z_index="0" medium_width="0" mobile_width="0" css_animation="left-t-right" width="1/1" uncode_shortcode_id="448469"][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h3" text_size="h3" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" sub_lead="yes" sub_reduced="yes" uncode_shortcode_id="186338" subheading="From a designers perspective, there are only a few types of developers we are likely to meet in our day-to-day operations:"]Different kinds of developers[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="165177"]Maintaining a system like this requires several different kinds of people with a variety of talents between them. Most developers are the most comfortable working on a single component of the system, which gives them all different titles and roles.[/vc_column_text][vc_single_image media="118976" media_width_percent="100" uncode_shortcode_id="257566"][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h5" text_size="h5" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" uncode_shortcode_id="190770"]Front end developers[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="658009"]Every one of us is collaborating with at least one front-end developer. These front-end technologies construct our layouts locally on the clients machine. They usually hold computer science or engineering degrees and are enthusiastic about robust and logical solutions. Things like quick loading times, secure data transfer, and robust data architecture.nnWe dont work directly with them, but their work can directly impact what we can design.[/vc_column_text][vc_custom_heading heading_semantic="h5" text_size="h5" text_weight="700" text_height="fontheight-108164" text_space="fontspace-111509" uncode_shortcode_id="537118"]Full stack developers[/vc_custom_heading][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id="943131"]Developers can work on both the front and back ends of a system. This allows users to have complete control over the look and feel of their websites by defining their preferred page structure, section roles, section contents, and element styles.nnAs an example, think about the text you just read. When this page loads, it looks like the image on the right when viewed in a web browser. text: Im Vedanshu Srivastava, a seasoned design leader with a decade of experience crafting exceptional digital experiences.
I thrive on the intersection of art and technology, where innovation meets intuition. My work is driven by a deep understanding of user behavior and a relentless pursuit of aesthetic excellence.

Whether its designing intuitive interfaces, crafting compelling brand stories, or leading cross-functional teams, Im dedicated to delivering exceptional results. Im excited about the future of design and the potential of AI to revolutionize the industry.
“ Through Swift Legal, we received expert advice and streamlined support, turning a daunting procedure into a smooth experience. ”

As a seasoned design leader with over a decade of global experience, Im passionate about crafting innovative, user-centric solutions that bridge the gap between business goals and user needs. My expertise lies in leveraging design thinking and research to create intuitive, delightful experiences across various channels. Ive successfully navigated complex challenges and delivered impactful results for renowned brands. My ability to collaborate across disciplines and embrace ambiguity allows me to drive innovation and create lasting value for businesses and their customers.

the-80-20-path-to-innovation-lessons-fro.title: the-80-20-path-to-innovation-lessons-from-gandhi
text: A strategic framework for creative problem-solving.

In a world overflowing with challenges, innovative solutions are the key to progress. But how do we consistently generate groundbreaking ideas? Renowned thinker and author, David Epstein, offers a fresh perspective on creative problem-solving, drawing inspiration from the life and work of Mahatma Gandhi.

Epstein introduces the concept of the “80/20 rule.” By focusing on the 20% of tasks that yield 80% of the results, we can maximize our impact and avoid getting bogged down in trivial details. This strategic approach, exemplified by Gandhi’s focus on nonviolent resistance, allows us to allocate resources efficiently and achieve significant outcomes.
Choice Mapping: A Deliberate Approach to Insight

Traditional brainstorming techniques often rely on spontaneous, unfiltered ideas. While this can be effective, Epstein advocates for a more structured approach called choice mapping. By systematically considering different options and their potential consequences, we can increase our chances of generating innovative solutions.
Learning from the Master: Gandhi’s Strategic Framework
Gandhi’s monumental challenge was to unite a diverse population and mobilize them against a powerful colonial force. To achieve this, he drew inspiration from various sources:
Inspired by the British women’s suffrage movement, Gandhi recognized the effectiveness of nonviolent protest.
Influenced by Tolstoy’s communal farms, Gandhi established ashrams to foster a sense of unity and shared purpose.
By incorporating traditional Indian elements into his movement, Gandhi resonated with the masses and legitimized his cause.

The Salt March, a pivotal moment in India’s history, showcased the culmination of Gandhi’s strategic thinking. By combining these disparate elements into a coherent framework, Gandhi revolutionized the landscape of political activism.
Identify the core elements of your problem and focus on solving them first.
Use choice mapping to systematically explore different options and their potential outcomes.
Study the successes and failures of others to gain insights into effective problem-solving strategies.
Combine seemingly unrelated concepts to create innovative solutions.
Use language and symbols that resonate with your target audience to build support and engagement.
Applying Gandhi’s Lessons to Modern Challenges.

History encourages us to adopt a similar approach to our own problem-solving endeavors. By carefully analyzing the problem, identifying key components, and drawing inspiration from diverse sources, we can develop innovative and effective solutions.

Whether you’re a business leader, a social entrepreneur, or an individual facing personal challenges, the principles outlined in this article can help you navigate complexity and achieve your goals. By embracing strategic thinking, prioritizing effectively, and learning from the past, we can shape a brighter future.

privacy-policy-2.title: privacy-policy-2
text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.
If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.
Who we share your data with
If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.
How long we retain your data

If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.
What rights you have over your data

If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.
Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

the-ai-powered-cx-singularity.title: the-ai-powered-cx-singularity
text: The tectonic plates of customer experience are shifting, and the epicenter? Artificial Intelligence. This isn’t a gentle tremor; it’s a full-blown seismic event reshaping the very landscape of engagement. We’re not talking about chatbots and automated replies; we’re witnessing the dawn of a hyper-intelligent, emotionally attuned era of customer interaction. Are you poised to ride this wave, or will you be swept away by its force?
Data Speaks: The Oracle Has Spoken.
Let’s dispense with the hypotheticals and dive into the irrefutable truth: AI is no longer a futuristic whisper, it’s the roaring engine of contemporary business.
Nearly Half of Tech Leaders (49%) Have Crossed the AI Rubicon:
This isn’t a trial run; it’s a full-scale integration. The message is clear: AI is no longer optional.
In a market defined by rapid growth and fierce competition, Generative AI isn’t just a tool, it’s a profit multiplier.
This isn’t theoretical; it’s tangible growth, directly attributable to the power of Gen AI. The age of speculation is over; the age of demonstrable results is here.
These figures aren’t just numbers; they’re a clarion call. The AI revolution isn’t coming; it’s already here, and it’s rewriting the rules of the game.
The Customer: A Digital Nomad with Exquisite Demands.
Today’s customer isn’t just a consumer; they’re a discerning digital nomad, demanding experiences that transcend the ordinary. They expect:
Preemptive Service: The Power of Prescience:
They crave solutions before they even articulate the problem, demanding a level of anticipation that borders on telepathy.
Hyper-Personalization: The Art of the Individual:
They expect experiences tailored to their unique digital fingerprint, a symphony of personalized interactions.
Emotional Resonance: The Language of Feeling:
They seek brands that understand their unspoken emotions, forging connections that resonate on a deeper level.
Omnichannel Orchestration: The Symphony of Seamlessness:
They demand a consistent, fluid experience across every touchpoint, a seamless journey through the digital ecosystem.
To meet these elevated expectations, businesses must wield AI like a master craftsman, sculpting experiences that are not just efficient, but profoundly human.
Unleashing the AI Kraken: Key Strategic Imperatives.
AI as the Architect of CX Renaissance:
AI isn’t just a tool; it’s a catalyst for a customer experience renaissance. It enables the creation of dynamic, responsive ecosystems that anticipate needs and exceed expectations.
The Ethical Compass: Navigating the AI Frontier:
Trust is the currency of the future. Responsible AI adoption, anchored in ethical principles and robust governance, is non-negotiable.
Empowering the Human Element: The AI-Augmented Workforce:
AI isn’t about replacing humans; it’s about empowering them. By automating the mundane, AI frees up human potential for creativity, empathy, and strategic problem-solving.
AI-Driven Business Alchemy: Forging New Paradigms:
AI is the alchemist of modern business, transforming traditional models into agile, customer-centric ecosystems like quick commerce and XaaS.
Beyond the Algorithm: The Soul of CX.

While AI provides the scaffolding, the human element remains the soul of customer experience. Humanized AI, capable of understanding and responding to emotional nuances, is crucial. But equally important is the strategic integration of human interaction, ensuring that technology enhances, rather than replaces, the human touch.
The Call to Action: Crafting Your AI Legacy.
To truly harness the transformative power of AI, businesses must adopt a strategic, culturally nuanced approach. This involves:
Developing a visionary AI strategy that aligns with core business objectives.
Building a robust data fortress, fortified by ethical governance.
Championing ethical AI practices, ensuring fairness and transparency.
Empowering your workforce with the tools and knowledge to thrive in the AI era.
Embracing a culture of continuous learning and optimization.
The AI revolution is not a spectator sport; it’s an active endeavor. Are you ready to architect your future?

But equally important is the strategic integration of human interaction, ensuring that technology enhances, rather than replaces, the human touch.

From Niche to Mainstream

rn

Using Everett Rogers’ diffusion of innovation model, the trajectory is clear. Technologies tip into mainstream adoption once they cross 20% penetration—the moment when early adopters give way to the early majority.

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Current usage (July 2025): 700 million weekly active users (WAU), up from 400 million in February.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Global TAM: 5.65 billion internet users.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Tipping point: 1.13 billion WAU.

    rn
    • rn
rn

At 11–12% month-over-month growth, ChatGPT could hit that figure by late 2025. Even with slower growth, the adoption curve projects mass usage between December 2025 and August 2026.

rn

For digital strategists, the timeline is compressed. We have months to prepare for an AI-first search world.

rnrnrn
rnrn

The Behavioral Shift Beneath the Surface

rn

OpenAI’s usage data reveals a striking behavioral pivot:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Asking (search/information seeking): 51.6%

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Doing (task execution/content creation): 34.6%

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Expressing (sharing thoughts): 13.8%

    rn
    • rn
rn

In other words: ChatGPT is no longer primarily a productivity assistant—it is becoming the default interface for search.

rn

User satisfaction is strongest in “Asking” queries, with a Good-to-Bad rating ratio of 4.45:1, outpacing other use cases.

rn

Topic analysis reinforces this:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    Practical guidance (29%) and information-seeking (24%) now dominate, while writing tasks have dropped from 36% in 2024 to 24% in 2025.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Within writing, two-thirds of tasks are now about refining existing text, not generating from scratch.

    rn
    • rn
rn

The pattern is unmistakable: information retrieval and decision support are overtaking content creation as the primary value of AI.

rnrnrn
rnrn

The Competitive Struggle Ahead

rn

Google, unsurprisingly, has responded with AI Mode, now live in 180 countries. This sets up a head-to-head battle:

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    OpenAI’s edge: Conversational search behavior already ingrained in millions of users.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    Google’s edge: Decades of search infrastructure, contextual authority, and a global ad ecosystem.

    rn
    • rn
rn

The stakes are existential. If Google cannot transition aggressively, it risks the same fate as earlier engines displaced by its own rise. The company’s recent moves—like testing new payment protocols—hint at preparation for a world where AI-first interfaces displace traditional SERPs and ad clicks.

rn

Regardless of which platform dominates, the outcome is clear: AI-mediated search will define the future of discovery.

rnrnrn
rnrn

Why AI Traffic Matters More Than It Looks

rn

Current AI referrals account for just 1–2% of site traffic, tempting some to dismiss it as marginal. This is short-sighted.

rnrn
    rn
  • rn

    AI interactions are about influence, not clicks. Many users get what they need without visiting a site—but they are still influenced by the brand surfaced in AI responses.

    rn
    • rn
  • rn

    When users do click, conversion intent is stronger. Our research shows AI-referred visitors often convert at higher rates than traditional search traffic.

    rn
    • rn
rn

Extrapolate forward: at 20–30% adoption, AI-driven visits could represent 5–10% of total traffic—with higher conversion density. That is strategically significant for any brand dependent on search visibility.

rn

The era of keyword-chasing SEO is fading. AI search demands new approaches:

    Build for “Asking.” Content should answer decision-driven queries, not just target keywords.

    rn

  2. rn

    Create answer objects. Modular, authoritative content blocks that AI can cite in responses.

    rn
    3. rn
  3. rn

    Prioritize depth and originality. Thin or derivative content will be deprioritized by AI systems.

    rn
    4. rn
  4. rn

    Maintain technical SEO discipline. Speed, structured data, and crawlability remain foundational.

The shift is less about gaming algorithms and more about building content ecosystems that AI trusts to inform decisions.

rn
